subject: Request: p50/p95 measurement carveout for KV-cache warmup (Epsilon Analytics)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Santos <emma@epsilon-analytics.com>, ops+epsilon@epsilon-analytics.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: p50/p95 measurement carveout for KV-cache warmup (Epsilon Analytics)

Hi Emma / Epsilon ops team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. We ran the end-to-end preview of your traffic pattern against the hosted endpoint overnight and surfaced a reproducible tail effect correlated with cold KV-cache warmup after infrequent model variant switching. Quick summary of the numbers from a 24h sample (attached CSV):

- Target commitment in the contract: p50 = 45ms, p95 = 420ms (rolling 24h measurement window)
- Observed steady-state (after warmup): p50 = 38ms, p95 = 360ms
- Observed at model-switch / cold-cache boundary (first 15 minutes after scale-up): p95 spikes to 920ms in our measurements (affects ~0.7% of requests during those windows)

We believe the spikes are operational (KV cache misses + model variant switching + prefix rehydration) and not representative of normal steady-state routing. To reduce risk of an SLO violation while we harden the warmup path, we propose a short-term exception: carve out a bounded warmup window per region/model-variant transition from p95 calculations (only for this account) for a 30-day period. Operational plan attached (proposed-carveout-wording.docx) and tech mitigation timeline:

1) Immediate: temporary carveout for warmup windows (<= 20 minutes per region per variant switch; gated by routing events).
2) Week 1–2: deploy KV-cache pre-warm for Epsilon's pinned variants + progressive rollout.
3) Week 3–4: replace reactive rehydration with async prefetch triggered by deployment hooks (reduces warmup p95 to <420ms).

Ask: please confirm you are comfortable with the carveout wording and we will file a formal SLO addendum. If you prefer, we can instead agree to an amended measurement window (rolling 24h excluding transient carveouts) — our legal & contracts teams will finalize whichever you choose.

Next steps: if you approve, I’ll loop in contracts to draft an addendum and Marissa will schedule the canary windows.

Thanks —
Jord

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kvcache-impact-brief.pdf, prod-latency-sample-20270320.csv, proposed-carveout-wording.docx
From: Emma Santos <emma@epsilon-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+epsilon@epsilon-analytics.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: p50/p95 measurement carveout for KV-cache warmup (Epsilon Analytics)

Thanks Jordan — useful write-up and appreciate the proposed timeline. A few quick clarifying Qs from my side before we escalate to legal: 

1) How many warmup windows did you observe in the 24h sample and what triggered them?
2) Will the carveout be account-scoped only (i.e., not applied platform-wide)?
3) Can you quantify user-facing error/latency impact (are these timeouts or degraded results)?

From our perspective we want something narrow and auditable — we cannot accept an open-ended carveout. If the proposal is bounded (per-variant switch, per-region, maximum of 20 minutes per event, capped at N events/day) then we can provisionally approve to unblock procurement.

Emma
Director of Product, Epsilon Analytics
emma@epsilon-analytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Santos <emma@epsilon-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: p50/p95 measurement carveout for KV-cache warmup (Epsilon Analytics)

Emma — thanks for the clear constraints. Jordan, below is the tightened carveout language we propose for legal review (we attached a DOCX in the original thread):

- Scope: carveout applies only to requests routed to Epsilon Analytics' dedicated model variants on Redwood-hosted endpoints.
- Trigger: carveout window begins when a model-variant transition occurs (e.g., variant roll, scale-up event, or routing change) and ends either after 20 minutes or when the per-route KV-cache hit-rate reaches 85%, whichever comes first.
- Cap: maximum of 4 carveout events per region per 24-hour period. Any additional events will be treated as normal traffic for SLO calculations.
- Review: carveout in effect for 30 calendar days from execution of addendum; both parties will meet at day 20 for an operational review.

We'll include an audit·log clause (timestamps and event ids) so the carveout is auditable by your ops team. Rishi — can you confirm instrumentation and whether dashboards for the carveout events can be provisioned by tomorrow?

Thanks,
Laura

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Emma Santos <emma@epsilon-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: p50/p95 measurement carveout for KV-cache warmup (Epsilon Analytics)

Emma / Team — quick technical confirmation:

- Instrumentation: we can emit a carveout_event entry to the account audit stream with event_id, region, model_variant, start_ts, end_ts, and KV-cache-hit-rate samples. This will be visible in the account's audit logs and a dedicated dashboard (I will share the Grafana link).
- Enforcement: the carveout is only applied in SLO calculation pipelines (metric-ingest), not in runtime routing. It is a measurement exclusion — you will continue to get served the same model variants.
- Limits: we can enforce the cap (4 events/region/day) via an automated policy that adds an 'extra_event' flag to the audit stream if exceeded.
- Timeline: can ship the dashboard and audit stream entries within 24 hours after we get confirmation to proceed.

We also did a small canary this morning where we pre-warmed the KV cache and observed peak p95 during warmup drop from 920ms to ~380ms. We'll document the canary notes and add them to the addendum appendix.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma — thanks for the prompt feedback and for being explicit about auditability. Per your constraints, here's the operational next step I will take once I get your green light: 

1) Draft a short SLO addendum capturing the exact language Laura proposed and the caps we discussed.
2) Hook Rishi's audit stream into the claim process so both sides can independently verify carveout events.
3) Schedule a 45-minute ops review on day 20 of the carveout (we propose Tue Apr 12, 2027) to decide on extension/cleanup actions.

If that works, Jordan — please mark this deal stage in HubSpot as "Carveout Approved - Addendum Drafting" and I'll create the DocuSign packet for signature. Emma — can you confirm by EOD today so we can hit procurement timelines?

Best,
Marissa
